chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Maymun ibn Mihran has been transmitted by me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Attar - may Allah be pleased with him - from his father, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Malik, from Abu Yahya Al-Ahwazi, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, the seller of shrouds, from Maymun ibn Mihran.

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى الْ: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Attar, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.بَيَّاعُ الْأَكْفَانِ: The seller of shrouds, a kunya (nickname) for Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I narrated it, indicating the author's direct transmission
key_terms.مَيْمُونُ بْنُ مِهْرَانَ: Maymun ibn Mihran, a prominent early Shia scholar and tabi'i

ai.seo_question: What is the chain of narrators for Maymun ibn Mihran in this text?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous methodology of *al-istifrad* (collecting all narrations) employed by Shaykh al-Saduq to distinguish between his personal recitations (*riwayatihi*) and those merely present in the text (*ma kana fihi*). By explicitly tracing the chain from Maymun ibn Mihran through Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Attar and subsequent narrators, al-Saduq provides essential epistemological transparency, allowing scholars to verify the reliability of the transmission line independently of the main text's compilation.
